paper.title: Joint Optimization of Wind Turbine Micrositing and Cabling in an Offshore Wind Farm

conflicts_and_completions: Equation 37 prints square-root of ten times rotor radius for spacing, but the native experiment explicitly uses the 500 m cell length; production uses 500 m.
Model 2 fixes 210 MW and Table VI reports 210 MW, while Fig. 7 labels its best-profit layout with 75 turbines; production uses 70 three-MW turbines.

Equation 37 includes AC-network constraints, but the stated inner QP in Eqs. 42-43 keeps active-power balance, reserve and generator bounds only; production implements the reproducible convex dispatch and does not claim AC-OPF.
Equation 43 names reserve Rs without a value; production declares a fixed 50 MW reserve, consistent with feasibility of all reported connection-bus cases.
The paper cites Yarpiz but does not identify a BPSO asset; production reconstructs standard sigmoid BPSO with the exact Table V coefficients over a seven-bit parent-edge encoding.
Parent choices are restricted to nodes closer to the substation, guaranteeing a radial connected tree; the decoder chooses the lowest daily-cost feasible cable type for each subtree flow.
The grid model is described while Eq. 33 uses capacity and coordinate variables; production uses one real key per grid cell plus a capacity key and stable top-N decoding.
YPEA126 does not fix the target reference division count; 14 divisions generate exactly the paper population of 120 directions for three objectives.

Winter/summer wind and load curves are digitized as deterministic 24-hour arrays. Missing economics, thrust and entrainment constants are versioned source-level completions and are not calibrated to match Tables VI-IX.
The paper gives no repeat count; the platform formal protocol uses 25 independent seeds.

strategy: one persistent all-core executor per optimization
parallel complete outer candidates with fixed-index result and work receipts
parallel dominance rows and reference-direction association
serial inner BPSO, wake and dispatch inside each candidate to prevent nested oversubscription
immutable problem tables, wind trigonometry inputs and reference directions
counter-keyed schedule-independent random events and ordered survivor commits
hpc.dominant_complexity: outer contexts times outer population-generations times inner BPSO population-iterations times turbine-count, plus 24 times turbine-count squared wake work
hpc.required_invariant: one-worker and all-worker roles, layouts, cable trees, objectives, work counts and scientific hash identity

claim_boundary: Source-backed flexible academic reconstruction of the target joint micrositing/cabling/grid problem, target NSGA-III/BPSO/QP method and every native paper role; not author source, original wind/grid/economic arrays, MATLAB trajectory or numerical replay.
